s5.title: 2481 Roboteers | Behind the Glass Mic'd Match | FRC REEFSCAPE 2025 Arkansas

bet.text: Pick up coral from the floor in any orientation, because the human player can roll it almost to the reef. The team had not known it could go quite that far.

demand.text: Fast coral cycles: the team found that floor pickup in any orientation would make cycle times significantly faster. For endgame it chose the deep cage because it is worth the most points.

cycle.text: The floor intake pushes coral into one orientation. The elevator goes to a preset level, the slide lines itself up from the reef tags without the driver, and the robot can shoot by itself when every set point is met.

endgame.text: The climber hooks the deep cage and brings it to the middle of the robot, at its centre of gravity. Two ratchets hold the robot up.

gave_up.text: The speaker says passive alignment can be a little faster than a motor, but the team struggled to come up with a passive design that worked.

changed.text: The climber motor was not strong enough to hold the robot, so two ratchets were added. The elevator went through many iterations to become more durable, including custom one-piece pulleys.

outcome.text: 47-4-0 in official play; won the Archimedes division; pick 1 of the Archimedes alliance on Einstein; ranked 11 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 105.95, Archimedes).

solves.text: Bought modules still needed customising and their wheels slipped

facts.text: A centre hub joins two gears, and swapping two gears changes the speed
Built for more traction on the carpet so wheel odometry is more accurate

functions.name: Elevator
functions.type: cascade elevator with belts and chains

facts.text: Belts and chains are used together, which helps with weight
Custom pulleys are one piece, where bought ones are three
Goes to preset levels; if the cameras see the robot is too far back it rises a little so coral still reaches the peg
Two Kraken X60s at about 6:1 drive an 18T #25 sprocket on both sides
The second stage uses 9 mm timing belts, which do not stretch much, on custom UHMW pulleys with big flanges
A constant force spring was added after the Arkansas event for speed; the ratio was about 8:1 before
Bought elevator blocks are fitted with 1/4-20 threaded shoulder bolts

cost.text: Many iterations and design changes to make it durable
Standard pulleys were dropped because their flanges kept falling off
The team calls keeping everything square and sturdy enough for its speed the biggest thing

solves.text: Hold the robot under a deep cage at its centre of gravity

facts.text: Brings the cage to the middle of the robot
Two ratchets hold the robot up and take stress off other parts

cost.text: The motor alone could not hold the robot

decisions.because: two seasons of bought modules still needed customising, and the wheels slipped
a slide had worked for the team in 2019
decisions.cost: passive devices can be a little faster

decisions.choice: Ramp and one motor in the intake
Belts and chains together in the elevator

decisions.because: it is worth the most points
